ai.title: Ad engagement end reason drops unknown values and adds expired
ai.summary: The ad engagement record in `common/src/types/ad-client-context.ts` adds `expired` to the `ENGAGEMENT_ENDED_BY` vocabulary, indicating an ad was taken off screen due to a wall-clock cap or away-time limit. The `endedBy` field now applies `.catch(undefined)` so that an unrecognized end reason is dropped from the record rather than causing the entire engagement record to fail parsing. This additive change allows newer clients to send the `expired` value before older servers that do not yet recognize it are updated, preserving the rest of the timing data in the record.

eli5.text: The ad tracking log now includes a new reason for why an ad disappears, specifically when it has been on screen for too long. Because of how these logs are processed, if a new version of the app sends a reason that an older server doesn't recognize, the server simply ignores that one missing detail instead of discarding the entire record. This ensures that timing data about how long an ad was shown is preserved even if parts of the information are new. There is no visible effect on your daily use of the coding assistant; this is a behind-the-scenes update that helps advertisers and the platform understand ad performance without causing errors.

ai.title: Add ad expiry clock to remove stale ads on screen
ai.summary: The CLI ad subsystem now enforces a maximum on-screen duration for all ad units. A new shared module `common/src/ads/ad-expiry.ts` defines the expiry limits (a hard cap of 2x the rotation interval, and an away limit of 1x), and a new CLI module `cli/src/ads/ad-expiry-clock.ts` tracks the first draw time of each impression by `impUrl`. When an ad exceeds these limits, the rotation tick plan in `use-gravity-ad.ts` now returns an `expire` action that clears the slot and drops expired response ads, preventing stale impressions from being re-shown from the cache.
ai.evidence: The diff introduces `common/src/ads/ad-expiry.ts` with `adExpired` and `adExpiryLimits` (using `AD_EXPIRY_DEFAULT_ROTATION_MS` of 180_000 and `AD_EXPIRY_CHECK_MS` of 15_000), and adds `cli/src/ads/ad-expiry-clock.ts` which tracks `impUrl` draw times, marking them expired if shown too long while idle or past the hard cap.
